quit.title: Quit {app}?
quit.message: Your friends will be disconnected from the world.
gui.core_unreachable: The {app} background service is not responding: {error}
gui.err.core: The {app} background service could not be reached.
host.title: Play your world with friends
host.intro: Your friends join your Minecraft world over the internet. Nothing to install on a server, nothing to configure on your router.
host.step_open_lan: In Minecraft, open your world, press Esc and choose "Open to LAN" → "Start LAN World".
host.step_send_code: Send the join code to your friends (WeChat, QQ, Discord… anything works).
host.mode_auto_hint: Detected automatically, even when its port changes.
host.mode_manual: A Minecraft server on this computer
host.mode_manual_hint: For a dedicated server. Enter its port:
host.world_waiting_hint: In Minecraft: press Esc → "Open to LAN" → "Start LAN World". It will be picked up automatically.
host.lan_detection_off: LAN worlds can't be detected on this computer (another program may be using the discovery port). Use "A Minecraft server on this computer" with the port Minecraft shows in chat instead.
host.server_missing: Nothing is listening on port {port} yet. Start your server, or check the port.
host.code_hint: Send this code to your friends. They paste it in {app} under Join. Anyone with the code can join while it is valid, so share it only with friends.
host.new_code_hint: "New code" makes the old one stop working.
host.approval_on: You approve every friend who joins (change in Settings).
host.reply_title: Did a friend send you a reply code?
host.reply_hint: If your friend's app says "one more step", it shows a reply code starting with LY1R-. Paste it here and both apps will connect at the same moment.
host.punching: Opening a direct path to a friend ({n} addresses)…
join.title: Join a friend's world
join.intro: Paste the join code your friend sent you (it starts with LY1-).
join.connecting_hint: This usually takes a few seconds.
join.need_reply_title: One more step: send this reply code to your friend
join.need_reply_text: Your friend's network doesn't accept incoming connections by itself. Send this reply code to your friend; they paste it in {app} under Host → "Did a friend send you a reply code?". Both apps then connect at the same moment.
join.waiting_approval: Waiting for your friend to let you in…
join.waiting_approval_hint: Your friend's {app} asks them to allow you.
join.connected_lan: In Minecraft, open Multiplayer. The world appears under "Scanning for games on your local network" as "{motd}".
join.connected_direct: If it doesn't show up, use "Direct Connection" with this address:
join.auth_note: {app} only forwards data. Minecraft accounts are checked by your friend's game, exactly like on a LAN.
strategy.peer-reflexive: Through the router (address learned from your friend)
clipboard.invite: A join code is on your clipboard. Join this world?
clipboard.reply: A reply code from a friend is on your clipboard.
update.err.not_configured: Update checks are not available in this build.
update.err.bad_signature: An update file did not have a valid signature and was ignored.
update.err.bad_manifest: The update information was invalid and was ignored.
diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.intro: Test what your network allows. Useful if friends can't connect.
diag.privacy: Nothing is ever sent anywhere automatically. Exported logs contain IP addresses; share them only if you want to.
diag.udp_blocked: No STUN server answered: UDP may be blocked
nat_hint.open: this computer has a public address.
nat_hint.restricted: friends can connect, sometimes with a reply code.
nat_hint.port_restricted: friends can connect, often with a reply code.
nat_hint.cone: friends can connect, possibly with a reply code.
nat_hint.symmetric: connections are hard; let a friend with a better network host, or enable UPnP.
cgnat.local_shared: Your internet provider shares one public address between many customers.
cgnat.router_private: Your router itself has no public address (your provider or a second router puts it behind another NAT).
cgnat.address_mismatch: Your router reports a different address than the internet sees (double NAT).
firewall.title: Windows Firewall
firewall.missing: {app} has no Windows Firewall rule yet. When you host, Windows will ask once.
firewall.blocked: Windows Firewall is blocking {app}. Friends can't reach you until you allow it.
firewall.banner_missing: Windows may ask whether {app} may use the network. Click "Allow access".
firewall.banner_blocked: Windows Firewall is blocking {app}, so friends can't connect to you.
firewall.guide_text: When you start hosting, Windows shows a window like this one:
firewall.illustration_alt: The Windows Security Alert window with both network boxes ticked and the Allow access button highlighted
firewall.step2: Also tick "Public networks" if your computer's network is set to Public (common on new PCs).
firewall.step3: Click "Allow access" (you may need an administrator password).
firewall.guide_blocked_text: Someone clicked "Cancel" on the Windows Firewall prompt earlier. To fix it:
firewall.blocked_step1: Click "Open firewall settings" below, then "Change settings".
firewall.blocked_step2: Find {app} in the list and tick both "Private" and "Public".
firewall.blocked_step3: Click OK and start hosting again.
firewall.installer_note: Tip: the {app} installer adds the firewall rule for you.
settings.title: Settings
settings.player_name_hint: Shown to the friend whose world you join.
settings.approval: Ask me before each friend joins
settings.approval_hint: When on, you click Allow or Deny for every join.
settings.updates_hint: Only tells you; nothing is downloaded or installed automatically.
settings.upnp: Ask my router to forward a port (UPnP, NAT-PMP, PCP)
settings.upnp_hint: Makes direct connections much more likely. Turn off only if your router misbehaves.
settings.manual_port_hint: Used for "A Minecraft server on this computer".
settings.udp_port_hint: Set a fixed port if you forward it manually on your router.
settings.guest_port: Local port for joined worlds (0 = automatic)
settings.guest_port_hint: The 127.0.0.1 port Minecraft connects to when you join.
settings.stun_hint: Used only to learn your public address. A mix of servers reachable from mainland China and elsewhere is queried in parallel.
settings.relay_future: A self-hosted relay for networks that can't connect directly is planned for version 1.1.
settings.reset_identity_confirm: All join codes you have shared will stop working. Continue?
settings.reset_identity_done: New identity created. Share a new join code.
settings.err.stunServers: Each STUN server must look like host:port (at most 20).
settings.err.udpPort: The UDP port must be 0 or between 1024 and 65535.
settings.err.guestPort: The local port must be 0 or between 1024 and 65535.
settings.err.manualPort: The server port must be between 1 and 65535.
settings.err.inviteHours: Join codes can be valid for 1 to 720 hours.
about.title: {app} {version}
about.text: Free and open source. Lets friends play Minecraft: Java Edition together over the internet, directly between your computers.
about.privacy: Privacy: there are no {app} servers. Your traffic goes directly to your friends, encrypted. No telemetry, ever. Public STUN servers only see your address when you host or join, and update checks (if enabled) only download a version file.
about.license: License: GNU GPL v3. Not an official Minecraft product; not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft.
err.host.not_running: You are not hosting right now.
err.host.busy: Please wait a moment, the code is being renewed.
err.host.udp_port: Could not open the network port. Is another program using it? (Settings → Advanced → Host UDP port)
err.host.listen: Could not start listening for friends.
err.host.no_network: No network connection found. Check that you are online.
err.host.no_such_guest: That friend is no longer connected.
err.reply.is_invite: That's a join code, not a reply code. Paste it under Join instead.
err.reply.invalid: That reply code is damaged. Ask your friend to copy it again.
err.reply.wrong_code: That reply code belongs to a different (or older) join code. Ask your friend to join again with your current code.
err.reply.expired: That reply code has expired. Ask your friend to try again.
err.code.not_code: That doesn't look like a join code. It should start with LY1-.
err.code.damaged: The code is incomplete or has a typo. Copy the whole code again.
err.code.newer_version: This code was made by a newer version of {app}. Please update.
err.code.is_reply: That's a reply code. Reply codes go to the host: paste it under Host.
err.code.expired: This join code has expired. Ask your friend for a new one.
diag.fail.cert_mismatch: The computer that answered is not your friend's. The code may be very old, or your friend reset their identity. Ask for a new code.
diag.fail.local_socket: {app} couldn't open a network connection on this computer.
diag.fail.bad_secret: This join code is no longer valid (your friend made a new one). Ask for the current code.
diag.fail.expired: This join code has expired. Ask your friend for a new one.
diag.fail.approval_timeout: Your friend didn't answer the join request in time.
diag.fail.version: Your {app} and your friend's are incompatible. Both of you should update.
diag.disconnected.lost: The connection to your friend was lost.
diag.disconnected.approval_timeout: Your friend didn't answer the join request in time.
diag.advice.send_reply: Send the reply code to your friend and ask them to paste it in {app} under Host.
diag.advice.udp_blocked: Your network seems to block the kind of traffic {app} needs (UDP). School, office and some public Wi-Fi networks do this. Try another network, such as a phone hotspot.
diag.advice.both_symmetric: Both of your routers are strict. A direct connection isn't possible between these two networks today. Try a different network for one of you (for example a phone hotspot), or use IPv6 if your providers offer it.
diag.advice.swap_host: Your friend's router is strict but yours isn't: let your friend join YOUR world instead (you host).
diag.advice.guest_symmetric: Your router is strict. Ask your friend to enable UPnP on their router (or forward a port), or try a different network yourself.
diag.advice.host_cgnat: Your friend's internet provider shares their public address (CGNAT). Ask the provider for a public IP address or IPv6, or let a friend host instead.
diag.advice.host_enable_upnp: Your friend can enable UPnP on their router (usually in the router's web page under "NAT", "Advanced" or "UPnP"). Then direct connections work.
diag.advice.ipv6_firewall: You both have IPv6, but a router firewall blocked it. The reply-code step usually solves this; otherwise check the IPv6 firewall settings on the routers.
diag.advice.ipv6_host_missing: Your connection supports IPv6 but your friend's doesn't. If their provider supports IPv6, enabling it on their router would let you connect directly.
diag.advice.ipv6_guest_missing: Your friend's connection supports IPv6 but yours doesn't. Enabling IPv6 on your router (if your provider supports it) would help.
diag.advice.host_firewall: Ask your friend to check that {app} is allowed in Windows Firewall ({app} → Diagnostics).
diag.advice.hotspot: As a quick test, connect one computer to a phone hotspot and try again.
diag.advice.relay_future: Networks like these will be supported by the self-hosted relay planned for {app} 1.1.
diag.host.good: Good news: your friends should be able to join directly.
diag.host.reply_likely: Friends can join, but sometimes they'll need to send you a reply code (their app will tell them).
diag.host.hard: Your router is strict, so many friends won't be able to connect. Enable UPnP on your router, or let a friend host.
diag.host.unknown: Your network type couldn't be determined. Friends can still try to join.
diag.host.udp_blocked: Your network seems to block the traffic {app} needs (UDP). Friends probably can't connect. Try another network.
diag.host.ipv6_ok: IPv6 works on your connection, which helps friends who also have IPv6.
